assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe matter as having mass and taking up space; it discusses density, which is a related but different concept.

copy.en:
Why does ice magically float on water?

Water is unique! Its solid state, ice, is about 9 percent less dense than its liquid state, causing it to float.
copy.tl:
Bakit lumulutang ang yelo sa tubig?

Kakaiba ang tubig! Ang solidong anyo nito, ang yelo, ay mga 9 porsyento less dense kaysa sa likidong anyo, kaya lumulutang ito.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga molutaw ang yelo sa tubig?

Lahi ang tubig! Ang solidong porma niini, ang yelo, mga 9 porsyento nga less dense kaysa likido, mao nga molutaw kini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Tiny calcium carbonate crystals in your inner ear shift to detect gravity!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify gravity as a non-contact force that affects the behaviors of materials and objects on Earth in predictable ways
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions gravity but only as a sensory detection mechanism in the inner ear, not as a non-contact force affecting the behavior of materials and objects on Earth. It does not support the competency's focus on gravity as a force.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Tiny calcium carbonate crystals in your inner ear shift to detect gravity!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the effects of gravity to the motion of an object
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe the effects of gravity on the motion of an object. It describes how the body senses gravity for balance, which is unrelated to the motion of objects under gravity.

copy.en: Tiny calcium carbonate crystals in your inner ear shift to detect gravity! This helps your brain maintain your physical balance and posture.
copy.tl: Ang maliliit na calcium carbonate crystals sa iyong inner ear ay gumagalaw para ma-detect ang gravity! Tumutulong ito sa utak na panatilihin ang balanse at postura.
copy.bis: Ang gagmay nga calcium carbonate crystals sa imong inner ear moalihok aron ma-detect ang gravity! Makatabang kini sa utok nga mapadayon ang balanse ug postura.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Styrofoam has trapped air pockets inside that make it a thermal insulator
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify advantageous and disadvantageous examples of conduction, convection, and radiation
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a thermal insulator, which relates to heat transfer, but it does not identify an advantageous or disadvantageous example of conduction, convection, or radiation specifically. It does not teach the modes of heat transfer or how to classify examples.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Styrofoam has trapped air pockets inside that make it a thermal insulator
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and identify sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy at school, at home and in the local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a use of a material related to heat energy (keeping drinks cold), but it does not observe or identify sources and uses of light, sound, or heat energy in the school, home, or community. It is a single example of insulation, not a broader identification of heat energy sources/uses.

copy.en: Styrofoam has trapped air pockets inside that make it a thermal insulator — perfect for keeping your drinks cold!
copy.tl: Ang Styrofoam ay may mga nakasara na air pockets na gumagana bilang thermal insulator — perfect para panatilihing malamig ang inumin mo!
copy.bis: Ang Styrofoam adunay mga nakaputos nga air pockets nga naghimo niini nga thermal insulator — perpekto sa pagpabugnaw sa imong ilimnon!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: chemical change called coagulation to form a solid clot when exposed to air
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why physical changes are reversible, and chemical changes are irreversible
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies coagulation as a chemical change but does not address reversibility or irreversibility, which is the core of G6-M-3. It only provides an example of a chemical change without explaining why chemical changes are irreversible.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: chemical change called coagulation to form a solid clot when exposed to air
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that the formation of new bonds or the breaking of existing bonds constitutes a chemical change and the formation of a new substance
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a chemical change and formation of a solid clot, but it does not explain bond breaking/formation or the general principle that new bonds/broken bonds constitute a chemical change. It is a specific example without the explanatory link required by G9-M-2.

copy.en:
What happens to blood when it touches air?

The Katipunan's blood compact signing used human blood, which undergoes a chemical change called coagulation to form a solid clot when exposed to air!
copy.tl:
Ano ang nangyayari sa dugo kapag nahawag sa hangin?

Sa paglagda ng dugo ng Katipunan, gumamit ng tunay na dugo na nagkakaroon ng chemical change na tinatawag na coagulation para maging solidong clot kapag na-expose sa hangin!
copy.bis:
Unsay mahitabo sa dugo kung mahawa sa hangin?

Sa pag-pirma sa dugo sa Katipunan, gigamit ang tinuod nga dugo nga moagi og chemical change nga gitawag og coagulation aron mahimong solidong clot kung ma-expose sa hangin!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your kidneys filter about 180 liters of blood every single day, removing waste and extra water to make urine!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a single fact about kidney filtration, but the competency requires using models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations to explain how body systems work together (e.g., digestion and excretion). No such representation or systems-integration explanation is present.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your kidneys filter about 180 liters of blood every single day, removing waste and extra water to make urine!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions kidney function, which is part of the excretory system, but G4-L-1 lists only muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory systems. Kidneys/excretory system are not among the listed systems, and the card does not describe how any of those systems work.

copy.en:
How much blood do your kidneys clean daily?

Your kidneys filter about 180 liters of blood every single day, removing waste and extra water to make urine!
copy.tl:
Gaano karaming dugo ang nililinis ng bato mo araw-araw?

Nagfi-filter ang mga bato mo ng halos 180 litro ng dugo bawat araw, tinatanggal ang basura at sobrang tubig bilang ihi!
copy.bis:
Pila ka litro nga dugo ang gihinloan sa imong kidney matag adlaw?

Ang imong kidney nag-filter ug mga 180 ka litro nga dugo matag adlaw, gikuha ang basura ug sobra nga tubig nga mahimong ihi!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: They undergo a physical change when dried into solid sheets.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain why physical changes are reversible, and chemical changes are irreversible
assignedReviews.reason: The card only states that drying kiping is a physical change; it does not explain why physical changes are reversible or why chemical changes are irreversible, which is the action of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: dried into solid sheets
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that matter has (exists in) three states called solids, liquids, and gases
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a solid state but does not identify the three states of matter (solid, liquid, gas) or teach that matter exists in these states. The mention of 'solid sheets' is incidental, not instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: made from ground rice! They undergo a physical change when dried into solid sheets.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe how changes in solid materials make them useful, such as when they are shaped, pressed, hammered, joined, or cut
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes drying, not shaping, pressing, hammering, joining, or cutting. Drying is not one of the listed changes that make solid materials useful, so it does not directly support this competency.

copy.en: Kiping leaf decorations for the Pahiyas Festival are made from ground rice! They undergo a physical change when dried into solid sheets.
copy.tl: Ang kiping leaf decorations para sa Pahiyas Festival ay gawa sa ground rice! Nagkakaroon ito ng physical change kapag pinatuyo at naging solid sheets.
copy.bis: Ang kiping leaf decorations para sa Pahiyas Festival gihimo gikan sa ground rice! Moagi kini og physical change kung mapauga ug mahimong solid sheets.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The pupil controls how much light enters, while the retina at the back converts that light into signals for your brain!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the eye's handling of light, but G4-L-1 specifically targets the muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory systems. The eye is not among these systems, so the card does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: How do your eyes handle light?
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses how the eye processes light, but G3-F-6 focuses on sources of light, how light behaves or can be changed, and its uses. The card does not describe light sources, behavior, or uses; it only mentions the eye's role in receiving light, which is not the competency's focus.

copy.en:
How do your eyes handle light?

The pupil controls how much light enters, while the retina at the back converts that light into signals for your brain!
copy.tl:
Paano pinoproseso ng mata mo ang liwanag?

Kinokontrol ng pupil kung gaano karaming liwanag ang papasok, habang kino-convert ng retina sa likod ang liwanag na ito into signals para sa utak!
copy.bis:
Giunsa pag-process sa imong mata ang kahayag?

Gikontrol sa pupil kung pila ka kahayag ang mosulod, samtang gina-convert sa retina sa likod kadtong kahayag ngadto sa signals para sa utok!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: because it lacks leaves for photosynthesis
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the process of photosynthesis and respiration, and identify its raw materials needed and products
assignedReviews.reason: The card only mentions the absence of leaves for photosynthesis as a reason for Rafflesia's nutrient absorption; it does not describe the process of photosynthesis or respiration, nor identify raw materials and products.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: absorbs liquid nutrients directly from its host vine's tissues
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain how some plants have adapted to unfavorable conditions in the environment, such as lack of rain or floods
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a parasitic nutritional adaptation, but it does not explain adaptation to unfavorable conditions such as lack of rain or floods, which is the focus of the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: absorbs liquid nutrients directly from its host vine's tissues
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card shows Rafflesia depending on a host vine for nutrients, but it does not explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet basic needs in the guided-example sense required.

copy.en: The Rafflesia flower absorbs liquid nutrients directly from its host vine's tissues because it lacks leaves for photosynthesis.
copy.tl: Ang Rafflesia flower ay sumisipsip ng liquid nutrients direkta mula sa host vine's tissues dahil wala itong dahon para sa photosynthesis.
copy.bis: Ang Rafflesia flower mo-absorb ug liquid nutrients direkta gikan sa host vine's tissues kay wala kini mga dahon para sa photosynthesis.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: complex liquid mixture
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that cobra venom is a liquid mixture, but it does not describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures such as solutions and suspensions. It only touches on the general concept of a mixture without supporting the specific competency.

copy.en: Philippine cobra venom is a complex liquid mixture with dissolved proteins and enzymes that disrupt prey nervous systems!
copy.tl: Ang venom ng Philippine cobra ay isang complex liquid mixture na may dissolved proteins at enzymes na gumagambala sa nervous system ng biktima!
copy.bis: Ang venom sa Philippine cobra usa ka complex liquid mixture nga adunay dissolved proteins ug enzymes nga makaguba sa nervous system sa biktima!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your liver filters liquid blood and uses chemical changes to break down toxic substances into harmless materials for your kidneys to excrete!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions liver and kidneys working together, but the competency requires using models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations to explain how body systems work together. The card uses none of these representations, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: uses chemical changes to break down toxic substances
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain that the formation of new bonds or the breaking of existing bonds constitutes a chemical change and the formation of a new substance
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions 'chemical changes' but does not explain that the formation or breaking of bonds constitutes a chemical change or the formation of a new substance. It only uses the phrase in passing about liver detoxification, not teaching the bonding concept.

copy.en: Your liver filters liquid blood and uses chemical changes to break down toxic substances into harmless materials for your kidneys to excrete!
copy.tl: Ang atay ay nagfifilter ng likidong dugo at gumagamit ng chemical change para hatiin ang toxic na bagay sa harmless materials na ilalabas ng kidneys!
copy.bis: Ang atay mo nagfilter sa likidong dugo ug naggamit og chemical changes aron buwagon ang toxic nga butang ngadto sa harmless materials nga ipagawas sa kidney!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It uses powerful superconducting magnets to align protons in the human body
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to identify the properties of magnets, including how they affect other magnets and objects made of different materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions magnets but does not teach properties of magnets, how they affect other magnets, or how they affect objects made of different materials. It only states that MRI uses superconducting magnets, which is not direct instructional support for the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It uses powerful superconducting magnets to align protons in the human body
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make a simple electromagnet and observe and record its properties
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not describe making a simple electromagnet or observing/recording its properties. It only mentions superconducting magnets in the context of MRI, which is not the same as constructing and investigating an electromagnet.

copy.en:
How does an MRI machine work?

It uses powerful superconducting magnets to align protons in the human body, creating detailed medical images without radiation!
copy.tl:
Paano gumagana ang MRI machine?

Gumagamit ito ng malalakas na superconducting magnets para i-align ang mga proton sa katawan, na gumagawa ng detalyadong medikal na larawan nang walang radiation!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagtrabaho sa MRI machine?

Naggamit kini og kusog nga superconducting magnets aron i-align ang mga proton sa lawas, nga nag-himo ug detalyadong medical images nga walay radiation!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: their mass stays exactly the same
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions mass but does not describe matter as anything that has mass and takes up space. It focuses on the distinction between mass and weight, not on the definition of matter.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: feels a change in weight due to gravity

assignedReviews.reason: The card references gravity affecting weight, but the competency specifically addresses gravity as a non-contact force affecting objects on Earth in predictable ways. The card is about the Moon and does not teach the Earth-focused behavior or the non-contact force concept directly.

copy.en: An astronaut traveling to the moon feels a change in weight due to gravity, but their mass stays exactly the same!
copy.tl: Ang astronaut na pumupunta sa buwan ay nakakaramdam ng pagbabago sa timbang dahil sa gravity, pero ang mass niya ay nananatiling pareho!
copy.bis: Ang astronaut nga moadto sa bulan makasinati og pag-usab sa timbang tungod sa gravity, apan ang iyang mass magpabilin nga pareho!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Crushing a solid medicine tablet into powder makes it dissolve much faster in water
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate how different factors affect the solubility of a solute in a given solvent, such as heat
assignedReviews.reason: The card addresses the rate of dissolution (how fast a solute dissolves) due to particle size, not the equilibrium solubility of a solute in a solvent. The competency focuses on factors affecting solubility, with heat as the example. Particle size affects dissolution kinetics, not solubility itself, so it does not directly teach the stated competency.

copy.en: Crushing a solid medicine tablet into powder makes it dissolve much faster in water for quicker body absorption!
copy.tl: Ang pagdurog ng solid medicine tablet sa pulbos ay nagpapabilis ng paglusaw nito sa tubig para sa mas mabilis na body absorption!
copy.bis: Ang pagdugmok sa solid medicine tablet ngadto sa pulbos makapadali sa paglusaw niini sa tubig alang sa mas paspas nga body absorption!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: This makes milk a liquid mixture called an emulsion.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe useful everyday examples of uniform and non-uniform mixtures, such as solutions and suspensions
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives an everyday example of a mixture (milk as an emulsion) but does not describe it as uniform or non-uniform, nor does it connect to solutions or suspensions as the competency requires. It only mentions the term 'emulsion' without explaining its classification or usefulness as a uniform/non-uniform mixture.

copy.en:
How tiny are the fat droplets in whole milk?

The fat droplets in whole milk are about 4 micrometers wide! This makes milk a liquid mixture called an emulsion.
copy.tl:
Gaano kaliit ang mga patak ng taba sa buong gatas?

Ang mga patak ng taba sa buong gatas ay mga 4 micrometer ang lapad! Kaya ang gatas ay isang likidong halo na tinatawag na emulsion.
copy.bis:
Pinaunsa kaliit ang mga patak sa tambok sa bug-os nga gatas?

Ang mga patak sa tambok sa bug-os nga gatas kay mga 4 micrometer ang gilapdon! Mao nga ang gatas usa ka likido nga halo nga gitawag og emulsion.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Halite, the mineral form of sodium chloride, is harvested from seawater
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that the non-living materials that make up the environment are referred to as 'earth materials'
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies halite as a mineral, which is a non-living material, but it does not teach the concept that non-living materials are referred to as 'earth materials'. It only gives a specific mineral example without addressing the target terminology or generalization.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: is harvested from seawater in the salt farms of Pangasinan
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: demonstrate various techniques in separating mixtures, such as decantation, winnowing, scooping, picking, evaporation, filtering, sieving, and using magnets
assignedReviews.reason: Harvesting halite from seawater involves evaporation, which is one listed separation technique, but the card does not demonstrate or explain any separation technique. It only states a source of halite, so it does not directly support the competency of demonstrating mixture separation techniques.

copy.en:
Where do we get halite?

Halite, the mineral form of sodium chloride, is harvested from seawater in the salt farms of Pangasinan!
copy.tl:
Saan natin kinukuha ang halite?

Kinukuha ang halite, isang anyong mineral ng sodium chloride, mula sa dagat sa mga salt farms ng Pangasinan!
copy.bis:
Asalin kuhaon ang halite?

Ang halite, mineral nga porma sa sodium chloride, gikuha gikan sa dagat sa mga salt farms sa Pangasinan!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Silica is a hard mineral that is also found in sand.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that the non-living materials that make up the environment are referred to as 'earth materials'
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a mineral (silica) but does not teach the concept that non-living materials are referred to as 'earth materials'. It does not use the term or explain the category.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Silica is a hard mineral that is also found in sand.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore the school grounds or the local area to observe or collect different types of rocks, describing their similarities and differences in terms of features, such as texture, color, and grain crystal size
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a mineral and sand, but does not involve observing or collecting rocks, nor describing similarities/differences in texture, color, or grain crystal size. It does not support the exploration activity.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Silica is a hard mineral that is also found in sand.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to locate and describe different types of non-living things found in and around their school, such as rocks, soil, water, air, metals, clouds, rain, and sunlight
assignedReviews.reason: The card identifies silica as a mineral found in sand, but does not guide locating or describing different types of non-living things in and around school. It is a single fact, not an activity or description of multiple non-living things.

copy.en:
What hard mineral is hiding in the rice for traditional sinukmani?

It contains silica in its husks! Silica is a hard mineral that is also found in sand.
copy.tl:
Anong matigas na mineral ang nakatago sa bigas ng tradisyonal na sinukmani?

May silica sa kanyang husk! Ang silica ay isang matigas na mineral na makikita rin sa buhangin.
copy.bis:
Unsa nga matagas nga mineral ang natago sa bugas sa tradisyonal nga sinukmani?

Naa nay silica sa iyang husk! Ang silica usa ka hugot nga mineral nga makita pud sa balas.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The full moon phase happens when the Earth is positioned directly between the Sun and the Moon
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: make drawings or a simple model to show the motion of the Earth and Moon relative to the Sun to explain the phases of the moon that people see from Earth
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a fact about the full moon alignment but does not involve making drawings or a simple model, nor does it show the motion of the Earth and Moon relative to the Sun. assignedReviews.card_evidence: The full moon phase happens when the Earth is positioned directly between the Sun and the Moon
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to carefully observe and describe the natural objects commonly seen in the sky during daytime and nighttime, including the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the Moon as a celestial object, but the competency requires guided activities to observe and describe natural objects in the sky, including the Sun, Moon, planets, and stars. This card provides a single factual statement about the full moon, not an observation or description of multiple celestial objects.

copy.en: The full moon phase happens when the Earth is positioned directly between the Sun and the Moon, fully illuminating the lunar surface!
copy.tl: Ang full moon phase ay nangyayari kapag ang Earth ay nasa gitna ng Sun at Moon, kaya buong-buo ang liwanag na tumatama sa lunar surface!
copy.bis: Ang full moon phase mahitabo kung ang Earth naa sa tunga-tunga sa Sun ug Moon, nga nag-illuminate sa tibuok lunar surface!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Doctors use giant magnets in MRI machines to scan your brain and check if your organs are healthy!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: carry out guided investigations to identify the properties of magnets, including how they affect other magnets and objects made of different materials
assignedReviews.reason: The card only mentions that MRI machines use giant magnets; it does not teach properties of magnets or how they affect other magnets or objects made of different materials, which is the core of the competency.

copy.en: Doctors use giant magnets in MRI machines to scan your brain and check if your organs are healthy!
copy.tl: Gumagamit ang mga doktor ng malalaking magnet sa MRI machines para i-scan ang utak mo at tingnan kung maayos ang mga organ mo!
copy.bis: Gigamit sa mga doktor ang dagkong magnet sa MRI machines aron i-scan ang imong utok ug susihon kung maayo ang imong mga organ!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Human muscles fatigue much faster at high mountain altitudes
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: Muscle fatigue at altitude is not muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory as a set.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The thinner atmospheric air delivers less oxygen to the bloodstream
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: Thin air is respiratory-adjacent, but the card never identifies nose, windpipe, and lungs.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: delivers less oxygen to the bloodstream
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: Less oxygen in the bloodstream at altitude is a condition, not identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels and how they work.

copy.en: Human muscles fatigue much faster at high mountain altitudes! The thinner atmospheric air delivers less oxygen to the bloodstream.
copy.tl: Ang mga kalamnan ng tao ay mabilis na napapagod sa matataas na bundok! Mas manipis ang hangin kaya mas kaunting oxygen ang napupunta sa dugo.
copy.bis: Ang mga kalamnan sa tawo dali ra kapoy sa taas nga kabukiran! Ang nipis nga hangin dili kaayo makahatag og oxygen sa dugo.
